params.body:
## Why

Every Stocklist page load and every card click logged this in the browser console on staging:

```
Alpine Expression Error: Unexpected token 'try'
Expression: "try { sessionStorage.setItem('ui-return', JSON.stringify({ vehicleId: 21718, ... })); } catch (e) {}"
Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'try'
```

An Alpine attribute holds an **expression**, not a statement. Alpine compiles the value into
`let __x = <value>` inside an `AsyncFunction`, and only a value that *starts with* `if (`, `let ` or
`const ` is wrapped in an async IIFE first (`rightSideSafeExpression` in its source). A bare
`try { ... } catch (e) {}` is therefore a syntax error, and a syntax error means the handler never
runs at all: no error at the click, just nothing happening.

## What broke

`resources/views/stocklist/_grid_card.blade.php` put exactly that statement in `@click`. So the
`ui-return` key was never written, and the companion code in `livewire/stocklist-browser.blade.php`
had nothing to read: returning from a vehicle to the list lost your scroll position and your page
size. The reader itself was fine, because it sits in `x-init`, which Alpine does wrap.

Both halves of the key now live in `resources/js/ui-return.js` as `window.uiReturn`
(`remember()` / `consume()`), next to the other globals the blades call (see `app.js`). A call is an
expression, the try/catch sits in the module, and a global survives every Livewire re-render of the
grid. Same key, same shape, same behaviour; the blade reads

```
@click="uiReturn.remember({{ $vehicle->id }}, $wire.perPage)"
```

## What else the sweep found

Every Blade attribute Alpine evaluates (`@…`, `x-on:`, `x-show`, `x-text`, `x-model`, `x-bind:`,
`:`/`::`) was grepped for a leading statement. **The card handler was the only broken one.** What the
grep also turns up and is deliberately left alone:

- `@input="if (van > tot) tot = van"` in the four range sliders (stocklist-browser,
  bidding-offer-browser, own-stock-list) and `x-on:beforeunload.window="if (dirty && …) { … }"` in
  vehicle-form: these start with `if (`, which is Alpine's own carve-out.
- `ownstock/_type_veld.blade.php:48` `@click="vt = 1; var s = …; s.dispatchEvent(…)"`: several
  statements, but the *first* one is an assignment, so the generated body parses. Ugly, not broken.
- `x-init` / `x-effect` / `x-data` take statements by design and were not touched.

`tests/Feature/AlpineExpressionTest.php` pins the rule: it greps the views for an Alpine attribute
that starts with a statement keyword Alpine does not wrap (`try`, `for`, `while`, `switch`, `do`,
`throw`, `var`, `return`, `function`, `class`) and asserts the card handler is a call. Both
assertions were mutation-checked: putting the old `try {` back makes them fail.

## Checked

- Real browser (Playwright) against the dev server on an own MySQL database, loaded from
  `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the post-2026-07-28 migrations the way CI does, with a
  fixture dealer, a logged-in user and four vehicles; database dropped afterwards.
  - The Stocklist page renders four cards, `window.uiReturn` is there, **zero console errors** and no
    Alpine expression error.
  - Clicking a card writes `{"vehicleId":21883,"perPage":20,"scrollY":400,"url":"/stocklist","t":…}`.
  - Following a card to its detail and coming back consumes the key (it is gone), restores the page
    size and scrolls the clicked card into view (`scrollY` 1240 instead of 0 on a fresh visit).
  - Still works after a Livewire re-render of the grid (favourites toggled off and on again).
  - The old shape was injected into the same live page as a control: it throws
    `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'try'` from `generateFunctionFromString` and writes nothing.
- `php artisan view:cache` + `php -l` on all 415 compiled views: clean.
- `npm run build` (public/build stays untracked).
- `php artisan test --filter='SmokeTest|StocklistBrowser|BuildContract|ClassReferencesResolve|Vehicle|AlpineExpression|CompiledViews|UiApiUsage|StylesheetSyntax'`:
  239 tests, 1257 assertions, 1 skipped, no failures.
params.title: Stocklist: the card click handler runs again
